I wrote the program in OCaml using only the standard library, and `node check.mjs` passes all 6 example cases.

I also tested it on generated input against a reference built from standard shell tools (`tr`, `sort`, `uniq`), and the output matched on 50 MB of random bytes. Timings for 50 MB inputs:

| Input | Time |
|---|---|
| Typical word text | 0.4s |
| Random bytes | 0.5s |
| About 5.5 million different words (worst case) | 1.7s |
| A single 50 MB word | 0.8s |
